acceptance: grep shows no direct chdb import outside the helper (tests may import the helper)
A unit test simulates a failing chdb native import and asserts os.getcwd() is unchanged afterwards
With a chdb that fails to load, tests/unit/test_standardized_test_commands.py and the local matrix tests no longer fail due to cwd
Upstream issue filed on the chdb GitHub repository (owner-approved) describing the missing try/finally around os.chdir in chdb/__init__.py; link recorded in context
context: Guardrails: G3 ledger unaffected (product fix). Evidence captured 2026-09-28 on Darwin 27 / Python 3.12.
description:
chdb/__init__.py:58-62 (chdb 4.1.6) does os.chdir(package_dir); from . import _chdb; os.chdir(cwd) with no try/finally. When the native load fails (the wheel fails dlopen on Darwin 27 with "mis-aligned LINKEDIT string pool"), the process cwd stays in site-packages/chdb. Observed effects: tests/unit/test_standardized_test_commands.py resolves Makefile under site-packages/chdb (42 failures); CLI subprocesses write results under the wrong cwd so tests/integration/test_local_platform_benchmark_matrix.py finds no result JSON; stray evil.duckdb and datafusion_working/ appear in site-packages/chdb and the repo root.

Implement one helper (e.g. benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/_dependencies.py) that saves cwd, imports chdb, and restores cwd in finally; route all sites through it. Enumerate with grep -rnE "import chdb|from chdb" benchbox tests scripts _project/scripts. Known sites: benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/_dependencies.py:16, client.py:91 (from chdb.session import Session), client.py:96, metadata.py:178, benchbox/core/tpchavoc/equivalence.py:1047. File an upstream chdb issue.
